thread:
Maria Chen: Quick sync — we need to lock down the networking lanes for Private deploy lifecycle planning. Customer asks keep coming: peering, NAT, and fully airgapped installs. Can we map priorities and minimal acceptance criteria?
Arjun Patel: +1. I suggest three lanes: 1) lightweight tenant peering (fastest), 2) customer-managed NAT/egress with IP preservation, 3) full airgap/offline installer.
Samira Ortiz: Field data — top customers (fintech, health) ask for airgap or strict egress control. Small ISVs prefer peering to avoid ops burden. We should capture SLA downgrade implications.
Devon Lee: Technical constraints: runtime needs to support both persistent peering sessions and transient NATed connections. Main risk is handshake and webhook callbacks in NAT scenarios.
Maria Chen: Good. Let's sketch minimal acceptance for each lane. I can take first draft.
Liam O'Connor: For peering lane, acceptance: TLS-mutual auth, route advertisement (BGP optional), 99.9% control-plane sync within 30s. Also document fallback to hosted endpoint.
Arjun Patel: For NAT lane, acceptance: preserved source IP (or stable SNAT range), port-forward capability, and an outbound webhook relay option. Need tests for stale NAT mappings.
Samira Ortiz: Airgap: offline installer (sha256 signed artifacts), local KMS support, and an operator-run upgrade path + rollback docs. Customers expect zero outbound.
Devon Lee: Implementation notes: we can reuse current handshake protocol but need an agent-side reverse tunnel for webhook-based callbacks. That should cover NAT without requiring cloud peering.
Maria Chen: Ok. Prioritization — field impact vs engineering effort. Quick wins = NAT + reverse tunnel (lower infra changes). Medium = peering (network team work). Long = airgap (packaging + security reviews).
Arjun Patel: Agree. Propose schedule: Q2 sprint 1: prototyping reverse-tunnel + tests. Sprint 2: NAT-edge beta with 2 customers. Q3: peering alpha. Q4: airgap pilot.
Samira Ortiz: Can we run a tiny customer advisory board for NAT beta? I have two willing customers (one fintech, one e-com).
Maria Chen: Please add them to the NDA list. Samira, can you get their network diagrams?
Samira Ortiz: On it.
Devon Lee: A couple of open engineering questions: 1) Should reverse tunnel be per-tenant or shared multi-tenant? 2) How do we handle KV cache locality if traffic is offloaded to customer network?
Arjun Patel: 1) per-tenant for isolation; maybe pooled for small tenants. 2) We'll document reduced cache hit expectations and offer explicit cache warm APIs.
Maria Chen: I'll create the spec PR with these lanes and acceptance criteria. Quick note: include metrics we care about: handshake latency, token egress counts, and upgrade fail rate.
JenkinsBot: build/privdeploy-specs #128 passed — artifacts uploaded to https://artifacts.redwood/privdeploy/specs-128.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
Liam O'Connor: UX/ops ask: we need clear rollback knobs for NAT beta — feature flags and a kill switch at routing layer. Add to spec.
Maria Chen: Noted. I'll add a rollback section with three tiers: ctrl-plane kill, agent unenroll, and package rollback.
Samira Ortiz: Field comms suggestion: two-page decision matrix for customers (which lane is best for them). I can draft.
Arjun Patel: Dev plan: I'll allocate two engineers for the reverse-tunnel POC. Devon, can you own NAT beta infra?
Devon Lee: Yup. Also will create a small test harness for flaky mappings.
Maria Chen: Thanks all. Action items: Arjun + Devon POC tasks, Samira customer diagrams + comms doc, Maria to open spec PR and timeline. We'll reconvene next Tue 10am. :calendar:
Liam O'Connor: :thumbsup:
